faq: Which platforms can you set up?
Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, Pinterest, Snapchat and Microsoft Advertising. Choose the ones you actually run or plan to run soon. Unused pixels only slow your pages down.
Do you need access to my ad accounts?
Yes, as a standard user or partner you invite in your own account. We never ask for passwords. We only need permission to read the pixel and set up events, not to spend money.
Will pixels slow my store down?
A little, since each one loads code. We install them the lightest way available and, with Standard and above, avoid duplicates. For many tags, ask about Tag Management so they load together.
Does this include running the ads?
No. This sets up the tracking that ads depend on. Campaign setup and management are separate services. We follow each platform's rules on data use, consent and what events may be sent.

desc:
Meta, TikTok and Google ad pixel installation gives each ad platform a clear view of what shoppers do in your store. Ecom Swift LLC installs and tests the pixels in your own accounts, so audiences, optimization and reporting run on clean data.

## What is an ad pixel, and why does it matter?

An ad pixel is a small piece of tracking code that tells an ad platform what a visitor did after clicking an ad. It reports page views, product views, add to cart, checkout starts and purchases back to Meta, TikTok or Google. Without it, the platform cannot tell which ads led to orders.

Ad platforms learn from the signals you send them. If the signals are missing, the system has little to optimize toward and your budget goes to people who only click. If the signals are duplicated or wrong, it learns the wrong lesson and reports sales that never happened.

## How clean pixel data affects your ad results

Ad delivery systems look for patterns among people who bought, then search for similar people. That only works when the purchase event arrives reliably, with the right value and currency. A pixel that fires twice per order doubles the revenue you see and makes every campaign look better than it is.

Pixels also feed your audiences. Visitors who viewed a product but did not buy can be shown it again, and past buyers can be excluded. None of this works when events are late, missing or tied to the wrong pages.

Server-side signals add a second path, because browsers and privacy tools can block scripts. The two paths must be matched so the same order is counted once.

## What a well-installed pixel setup includes

- One pixel or tag per ad account, installed once and never pasted twice into the theme.
- Standard events with the names each platform expects, so its tools recognize them.
- Product details on events, such as item ID, name, price and quantity.
- Purchase events that carry order value and currency, fired only on the order confirmation.
- A catalog link so dynamic product ads can use the same item IDs your events send.
- Deduplication between browser and server events, using a shared event ID.
- Tests in each platform's own checking tool, not only in a browser extension.
- Clean ownership: the pixel sits in your ad account, with your business as owner.
- Written install notes that say what fires, where and why.

## How we install and test your pixels

We start by looking at what already runs on your store, because old pixels from past agencies often fire alongside new ones. We remove what is duplicated, then install the pixel for each platform you use through your theme settings, your store's built-in channel, or Google Tag Manager, whichever fits your setup.

Next we pass the shopper events: page view, product view, add to cart, checkout and purchase. We walk through the store as a shopper would, and watch each event arrive in Meta's Events Manager, TikTok's Events Manager and Google's Tag Assistant. When an event shows twice or arrives without a value, we fix the cause and test again.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many platforms we cover, how many events we pass, and whether we add server events, starter audiences and a test purchase on each platform. You receive install notes at the end, so the next person who touches the store knows what is in place.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Create your ad accounts and pixels under your own business, so you always own them.
- Keep one source of truth for each pixel, either the theme or a tag manager, never both.
- Send the purchase value and currency with every order.
- Retest after a theme change, a checkout change or a new app install.
- Check events in the platform's test tool before you spend on ads.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting the same pixel code into several places in the theme.
- Adding a new pixel on top of an old one without removing the old one.
- Starting campaigns before the purchase event has been tested.
- Letting an agency own the pixel inside their own business account.
- Judging ad results from numbers you have not checked against real orders.

## Who ad pixel setup is for

This service suits a store owner about to run the first paid campaign who wants tracking right from day one. It also suits sellers whose Meta or TikTok numbers look far from their order list, and teams moving to a new theme or checkout.

It is a setup service, not ad management. You or your media buyer run the campaigns.

## What we need from you

Tell us which ad platforms you use or plan to use, and give us access to each ad account and your store as a collaborator, staff member, partner or developer user, depending on what the platform supports. If you do not have the accounts yet, we can guide you through creating them under your own business. We never need your passwords, and you can remove our access whenever the work is finished.
